findings.suggested_fix: Split compound criteria, replace subjective terms with observable outcomes, and state how each is verified.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Replace the requests/tool_calls/request_limit dict-key discriminator with a signal that is unique to the budget path (e.g. match on __cause__ being a UsageLimitExceeded, or introduce a dedicated typed budget exception), because interpret_failure enriches every typed LLMError with an identically-shaped failure_usage diagnostic.
evidence: Plan: 'Budget exhaustion is identified as an LLMRunnerError carrying a step-budget diagnostic (the shape interpret_failure attaches at structured_run.py:95-103: a dict with requests/tool_calls/request_limit keys), not by message text ... so unrelated LLMRunnerErrors ... keep propagating unchanged.'

structured_run.py:105-109 — the typed-LLMError branch does `exc.diagnostic = usage_log.failure_usage(run_messages, request_limit=..., tool_calls_limit=...)`, the SAME builder used for budget_diag at line 79/95-100.
usage_log.py:159-190 — failure_usage ALWAYS returns requests/tool_calls/request_limit/tool_calls_limit, so budget and non-budget diagnostics are shape-identical.
The only branch-specific discriminator is the budget error's `__cause__` (a pydantic_ai UsageLimitExceeded via `raise budget_err from exc`, structured_run.py:101), not the dict key-set.
findings.finding: The plan's budget-exhaustion predicate (LLMRunnerError carrying a dict with requests/tool_calls/request_limit keys) cannot distinguish a real step-budget exhaustion from other typed LLMRunnerErrors, because interpret_failure's typed-LLMError branch enriches EVERY LLMError with a .diagnostic built by the same usage_log.failure_usage(...), yielding an identical key-set.
findings.location: Approach section ('a typed-plus-diagnostic check ... a dict with requests/tool_calls/request_limit keys'); structured_run.py:95-110; usage_log.py:159-190
scenarios: A non-UnretryableOutputError typed LLMRunnerError (e.g. a bare StructuredOutputError or an LLMRunnerError re-raised through branch 2) reaches the new except arm carrying a matching-shape diagnostic and is wrongly routed into recovery.
AC-2's negative control passes only for LLMRunnerErrors that lack ANY diagnostic; a non-budget typed error that DID run and got enriched would fail the intended propagation.
findings.suggested_fix: Identify budget exhaustion by its cause (isinstance(exc.__cause__, pydantic_ai.exceptions.UsageLimitExceeded)) rather than by the diagnostic key-set; or, cleaner, have structured_run.py raise a dedicated typed exception for the step-budget stop so CompletionAgentStep.run can catch it purely by type and drop the shape-sniff.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Specify a discriminator that actually distinguishes a step-budget exhaustion from other interpreted LLMRunnerErrors (which all carry the identical failure_usage key set), and reconcile it with AC-2's negative control.
evidence: Plan: 'Budget exhaustion is identified as an `LLMRunnerError` carrying a step-budget `diagnostic` ... a dict with `requests`/`tool_calls`/`request_limit` keys), not by message text — a typed-plus-diagnostic check, so unrelated `LLMRunnerError`s (e.g. config errors) keep propagating unchanged.'

structured_run.py:79 attaches the budget diagnostic via `budget_diag = usage_log.failure_usage(...)`; structured_run.py:105 attaches `exc.diagnostic = usage_log.failure_usage(...)` on ANY `LLMError` — the SAME function, SAME key shape.
usage_log.py:185-191: failure_usage always returns a dict containing `requests`, `tool_calls`, `request_limit`, `tool_calls_limit` — independent of whether the failure was a budget stop.

errors.py:29-45: `LLMRunnerError`/`StructuredOutputError` are `LLMError` subclasses, so a non-budget runner failure flowing through interpret_failure carries a diagnostic with the exact keys the plan checks for.

AC-2 requires: 'an `LLMRunnerError` without the step-budget diagnostic still propagates unchanged' — but under the specified key-shape check, essentially every interpreted `LLMRunnerError` WOULD carry those keys, so the negative-control the plan promises cannot be honored by the rule as written.
findings.finding: The plan's proposed discriminator for routing a caught LLMRunnerError into recovery — 'a dict with requests/tool_calls/request_limit keys' — does not actually distinguish a step-budget exhaustion from any other typed LLMRunnerError, because interpret_failure attaches the SAME failure_usage() diagnostic (same key set) to every LLMError it re-raises, not only the budget one.
scenarios: A non-budget StructuredOutputError/LLMRunnerError raised by the primary evidence step is caught, matches the key-shape predicate, and is wrongly routed into recovery instead of propagating.
The negative-control test (AC-2) cannot be constructed to both flow through interpret_failure AND lack the requests/tool_calls/request_limit keys, because interpret_failure always adds them.
findings.suggested_fix: Key the recovery route off a signal unique to the budget branch — e.g. a distinguishing finish_reason/marker set on budget_diag at structured_run.py:79-100, or an explicit budget flag/subclass — rather than the presence of requests/tool_calls/request_limit keys, since interpret_failure attaches those same keys to every typed LLMError.
